explanations: terra: A storm from the sky contains darknesses, thunder, and lightning, supplying the clouded and unstable opposite of the source's clear bright day and continuing in 2:20.
terra: Intermittent lightning lets people walk, while darkness makes them stand still; unstable flashes and enforced stillness contrast with steady ḍuḥā and settled, enduring night.

luna: The section develops the night-day succession as a recurring sign and links it with remembrance and gratitude. This verse names the alternation of night and day among signs, alongside rain, winds, and provision, placing the cycle within a larger pattern of sustenance. | terra: The alternation of night and day is included among concrete created signs for those who reason, giving the image its wider cosmic setting.
terra: Within the fasting night's own context, spouses are called garments for one another; night and clothing thus meet in an image of mutual nearness, shelter, and concealment.
terra: The new moons are declared time-markers for people, adding another Quranic meeting of nocturnal light with the naming and measuring of time.

luna: The source's night and duha succeed one another. This verse says God “causes the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night” (تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ), describing the transition as an ongoing interweaving. | terra: God inserts night into day and day into night, a direct account of the cover and light entering one another rather than either being lost.

luna: The image turns on two alternating times. This verse names the variation of night and day as a sign for people of understanding, extending the source's daily scene into reflection on the created order. | terra: The alternation of night and day stands among signs for people of understanding, supporting the section's reading of their order as intelligible address.
terra: God creates the darknesses and the light; their darkness-first order provides a broad cosmic reversal of 93's light-first opening.
terra: Whatever سَكَنَ in night and day belongs to God; its S-K-N wording echoes the source's definition of سَجَىٰ and places all settled things within both times.

luna: The section's night is a covering and repose, not an ending or abandonment. This verse speaks of God taking people at night, knowing their daytime acts, then raising them by day; it makes the night's covering temporary within an ongoing relation to God. | terra: God takes people by night and raises them again by day, so the nightly cessation preserves rather than abandons what will awaken.
terra: Night جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ, covered Abraham, and he saw a star within it; the scene directly combines an enclosing night with light that remains visible under the cover.
terra: Abraham next sees the moon rising and then setting, extending 6:76's covered-night scene through the appearance and disappearance of its greater light.
terra: Abraham then sees the sun rising and later setting; this completes the star-moon-sun passage and makes even the largest daylight source subject to arrival and withdrawal.

luna: The section pairs morning light with a night that has settled into quiet. This verse joins the dawn split from darkness (فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ), night as “rest” (سَكَنًا), and sun and moon as measures, showing the transition as both repose and ordered time. | terra: God cleaves daybreak, makes night سَكَنًۭا, and sets sun and moon for reckoning, joining emerging light, settled night, and measured time.
terra: Clothing is said to cover nakedness and provide adornment, supplying the concrete covering function that makes night as لِبَاس intelligible.

luna: The section's secondary cloth image shows night covering what remains beneath it. Here “the night covers the day” (يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ) and follows it swiftly, giving the covering a clear day-to-night movement. | terra: Night covers day in a rapid pursuit; the same covering scene also sharpens how unusual 93's motionless, lingering سَجَىٰ is.
terra: The towns are asked whether punishment might reach them by night while they sleep; it supplies the night-and-repose half of the deliberate pair completed by the forenoon scene in 7:98.
terra: The same temporal noun ضُحًۭى marks the forenoon when punishment might arrive as people play, showing that the bright hour does not by itself guarantee safety.

luna: The section describes duha as the sun's unobstructed spreading brightness and also notes a night bright like duha. This verse calls the sun's light ضِيَاءً and the moon's نُورًا, distinguishing daylight radiance from a light visible in the night sky. | terra: The sun is made radiance and the moon light, with phases for counting years; it joins bright day, luminous night, and time's measure in one ordered scene.

luna: The section treats the regular change between night and day as purposeful. This verse calls their alternation, together with creation in the heavens and earth, a sign for the mindful. | terra: The alternation of night and day is a sign for the mindful, so their repeated exchange carries meaning rather than marking abandonment.
terra: Dark pieces of night are said to cover condemned faces; night becomes almost material cloth here, while its punitive use reverses the section's sheltering calm.

luna: The source describes سَجَىٰ as both becoming still and remaining settled. Here God made night so people “may rest in it” (لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ) and day visible, grounding the night’s quiet in its function. | terra: God makes night so people may تَسْكُنُوا۟ in it and day visible; the S-K-N verb is the very definition used in the source to hear stillness behind سَجَىٰ.
terra: Even when people cover themselves with garments, God knows what they hide and disclose; a cloth cover therefore cannot entail divine absence or lost knowledge.
terra: Lot is told to travel in the night and that the appointed morning is near; the dark interval carries divine care toward an assured morning.

luna: The source's night acts like a covering over the day. This verse likewise says God “covers the day with night” (يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ), placing the same visual transition in a description of the earth's signs. | terra: God يُغْشِى ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ, another direct formulation of night laid over day as a covering.
terra: God equally knows one hidden by night and one going openly by day, so nocturnal cover never entails divine absence or concealment from Him.
terra: Lightning that brings fear and hope appears with heavy clouds, a cloud-borne and unstable brightness that bounds the source dictionary's cloudless light.
terra: Created shadows prostrate morning and evening, making their daily change a visible response to the same moving light that extends and retracts cover.

luna: The section pairs duha and settled night as two phases of a regular order. This verse names the sun and moon's continuing courses and says night and day are made serviceable, joining the image's lights and times to provision. | terra: Sun and moon are subjected دَآئِبَيْنِ and night and day are subjected for people, making persistence and regular service features of the same cycle.

luna: The source stages sunlight, night, and their succession. This verse groups night and day with the sun, moon, and stars, all made subject to God's command, presenting the same celestial scene as an ordered sign. | terra: Night, day, sun, and moon are all subjected by God's command and offered as signs, grounding both illumination and cover in one governance.
terra: The shadows of created things incline right and left in humble prostration, another concrete formulation of cover changing position under ordered light.
terra: God makes shade, shelters, and garments that protect from heat, supplying protective forms of cover at the bodily boundary of unobstructed sunlight.

luna: The source contrasts unclouded daylight with the opposing night and notes النهار as a daylight echo of the root behind 93:10. This verse calls night a sign whose light is erased and day a sign made visible (مَحَوْنَا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَا آيَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً), sharpening the boundary between obscurity and illumination. | terra: The night sign is effaced and the day sign made مُبْصِرَةً so people seek bounty and count time; darkness and visible light remain purposeful paired signs.
terra: The identical prohibition وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا uses نهر in the same sense, forbidding rebuke of parents as 93:10 forbids rebuke of the asker.
terra: The commanded span from the sun's decline through night darkness to dawn recitation lays out the transitions by which daylight closes and reopens.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to keep an extra vigil during part of the night, a deliberate waking use that marks the boundary of night as ordinary repose.
terra: At the cave, the rising sun inclines away and the setting sun passes aside, showing daylight physically redirected rather than spread without obstruction.
terra: At sunrise a people have no سِتْرًۭا from the sun, a concrete scene of unobstructed light that also supplies the opposite boundary to night as cover.
terra: The descending messengers speak only by the Lord's command and say that the Lord is not forgetful, a direct parallel to speech entering an apparent silence to deny abandonment.

luna: The section explains ضحى as both sunlight and the hour named after it. Moses sets the gathering for “the forenoon” (ضُحًى), using that specific daylight interval as a time marker. | terra: Moses fixes the public gathering for ضُحًۭى on the festival day, using the source word in its straightforward sense as a named, fully visible hour.

terra: Voices are hushed before the Merciful until only a whisper is heard; this may parallel the source's secondary detail of a sound-stilled world, though the ayah's scene is resurrection rather than night.
terra: Paradise promises that one will not تَضْحَىٰ, suffer exposure to the sun; this verbal branch of ض ح و marks the bodily limit of the section's welcomed morning brightness.

terra: The Prophet is told to glorify before sunrise and sunset, during night, and at the day's edges so that he may be content, joining the full light-dark cycle to the same addressee's promised رضا.
terra: God creates night, day, sun, and moon, each moving in an orbit; the two states belong to a continuous ordered motion.
terra: The question who can guard people by night and day locates protection through both times in the Merciful, making the cycle's security an act of continuing care.

luna: The section's image depends on day and night yielding to each other. This verse states that God causes night to enter day and day to enter night (يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ), placing the cycle within God's just ordering. | terra: God's insertion of night into day and day into night presents their changing lengths as deliberate action under the One who hears and sees.
terra: Life, death, and the alternation of night and day are placed together under God's agency, making each cessation part of a governed return.

terra: Cloud above layered sea and waves produces darkness in which a hand is scarcely visible; this is the exact atmospheric reverse of the source's dictionary sense of cloudless, unobstructed light.
terra: Piled cloud, hail, and nearly blinding lightning place brilliant light inside cloud itself, a specific boundary to the dictionary image of light with no cloud intervening.

luna: The section presents night and day as a recurring succession rather than a fixed state. This verse says God turns night and day (يُقَلِّبُ اللَّهُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ) and calls that change a lesson for those who see. | terra: God alternates night and day and calls that alternation a lesson for people of sight, closely matching the section's reflective use of the two times.
terra: God extends the shade, could have made it سَاكِنًۭا, and makes the sun its guide; moving light and potentially still cover meet in one measured scene.
terra: God then draws the extended shade back gradually, completing 25:45's sun-guided scene and showing a cover removed by degrees.

luna: The source hears the night as a settled covering, with morning light returning. This verse calls night “a garment” (لِبَاسًا), sleep a rest, and day “a rising” (نُشُورًا), giving the image a bodily cycle of covering, rest, and renewed activity. | terra: One ayah makes night a garment, sleep repose, and day نُشُورًۭا; the covering is temporary and the covered sleeper rises again.

luna: The source's bright day and potentially luminous night both belong to a changing sky. This verse places a lamp and a luminous moon (سِرَاجًا وَقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا) among the signs of the heavens, extending the image to the night sky's light. | terra: God places a lamp and an illuminating moon in the sky, furnishing a concrete nocturnal light for the source dictionary's bright-night sense.

luna: The source calls the regular change between duha and settled night purposeful. This verse makes night and day “following one another” (خِلْفَةً) for remembrance or gratitude, spelling out the purpose of their alternation. | terra: Night and day are made خِلْفَةًۭ for remembrance or gratitude, stating the purpose that the section finds in their regular succession.

luna: The section describes night as still and settled, with day returning to light. This verse says night was made so people “may rest in it” (لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ) and day “giving sight” (مُبْصِرًا), naming the complementary functions of the two states. | terra: Night is made for rest and day مُبْصِرًا; the paired gifts reproduce the still cover and unobstructed visibility of the section.

luna: The source pairs night with daylight as a regular change. This verse asks who could bring light (بِضِيَاءٍ) if night were made perpetual, imagining the boundary failing and making the value of returning daylight visible. | terra: The counterfactual of unending night asks who could bring light; it marks the boundary where a removable cover would become permanent and confirms that light's return is divine provision.

luna: The source's night gives way to duha and day. This verse asks who could bring night for rest if day were made perpetual (بِلَيْلٍ تَسْكُنُونَ فِيهِ), reversing the cycle and showing why the night boundary matters. | terra: The counterfactual of unending day asks who could bring a night in which people rest, showing that unbroken brightness would also violate the merciful alternation.

luna: The section makes the alternation between night and day purposeful. This verse calls it mercy: rest in the night, seeking bounty by day, and gratitude (لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ). | terra: Night for rest and day for seeking bounty are explicitly made from mercy so that people may give thanks, gathering the section's repose, provision, and gratitude.

luna: The source presents two times with different qualities. This verse places sleep in night and day and seeking God's bounty alongside them, treating their alternation as a sign that shapes human life. | terra: Sleep by night and day and seeking God's bounty are paired signs, widening repose beyond darkness while keeping rest and provision in the daily order.

terra: God spreads cloud across the sky before breaking it into fragments and bringing rain; this may invert the dictionary's spreading, cloudless light, though the ayah does not say the cloud dims the sun.

luna: The source's two times alternate in a measured order. This verse describes night entering day and day entering night, then says the sun and moon each run to an appointed term (كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى), linking the cycle to measured duration. | terra: Night enters day and day enters night while sun and moon run to fixed terms, joining extension of the two times to measured celestial order.

luna: The section makes the succession of light and night perceptible as an ordered change. This verse says night enters day and day enters night, with sun and moon each running to a term, extending that temporal order to the heavenly lights. | terra: Night and day enter one another as sun and moon run to appointed terms, another formulation of the regular, removable covering central to the section.

luna: The source imagines night as a covering over a world that has not disappeared. This verse reverses the action: God “strips the day from it” (نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ), leaving people in darkness, a concrete account of night arriving by the removal of daylight. | terra: God strips day from night, whereupon people are in darkness; this concrete removal makes light's disappearance a reversible covering action rather than a void.

luna: The source describes duha as the sun's rising light and the night as its counterpart. This verse says “the sun runs to its resting place” (وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا), placing that daylight within a larger ordered course.

luna: The source's night and day are successive, distinct states. This verse says neither sun overtakes the moon nor night precedes day (وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ), adding a boundary that keeps the cycle ordered. | terra: Night cannot outstrip day and every luminary moves in an orbit, setting a firm boundary around their reliable succession.
terra: The mountains glorify with David at evening and إِشْرَاق, sunrise brightness, giving the spreading morning hour a responsive created scene.

luna: The source presents night and day as successive coverings. This verse says God “wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night” (يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ), making their reciprocal covering a continuous cycle. | terra: God wraps night over day and day over night, so each covering is laid on and removed by the reciprocal cosmic order.
terra: One who devoutly stands and prostrates through hours of night inhabits the resting time in wakeful worship, while still relying on its distinctive quiet.
terra: God takes souls in death and sleep, retains some and releases others; it makes sleep a temporary holding whose release clarifies how covering need not be loss.

luna: The section's quiet night is a settled state rather than an absence. This verse again says night is for resting and day for seeing (لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا), making that quiet part of a recurring divine provision. | terra: God makes night for rest and day visible, then calls this divine bounty and notes how few give thanks, joining the image to the surah's thankful close.
terra: Night and day, along with sun and moon, are God's signs; the ayah directs worship past the visible times to their Creator.
terra: The clear Book is sent down in a blessed night, a second direct formulation of revelatory presence entering nocturnal stillness.

luna: The source links the recurring night-day sequence to remembrance and gratitude. This verse places night-day variation beside rain and the changing winds as signs, relating the cycle to provision from the sky and earth. | terra: Night-day alternation is joined to life-giving provision from heaven and called a sign for those who reason, linking the cycle to provision rather than withdrawal.
terra: The Prophet is told to be patient and glorify before sunrise and sunset, placing reassurance and praise at both visible boundaries of the day.
terra: The command continues with glorification during the night, completing 50:39's sunrise-sunset frame with the covered interval itself.
terra: The righteous sleep only a little of the night, explicitly reversing the usual repose and continuing toward their dawn practice in 51:18.
terra: At the approach of dawn the same people seek forgiveness, completing 51:17's wakeful night with an action at the edge where night yields to morning.

terra: The Prophet is told to await his Lord's judgment because he is under divine eyes and to glorify on rising; this directly answers apparent silence with watchful care and leads into the night scene of 52:49.
terra: Glorification during the night continues until the stars withdraw, joining a wakeful night to the visible boundary where its cover lifts.
terra: Sun and moon move by precise calculation, supporting the section's treatment of bright times and their extension as measured rather than accidental.

luna: The source's quiet night is one phase of a continuing day-night change. This verse says God causes night to enter day and day to enter night (يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ), making the transition part of divine knowledge and governance. | terra: God inserts night into day and day into night and knows what hearts contain; cosmic covering therefore never implies divine absence or ignorance.

terra: People cover themselves with their garments to refuse Noah's call; this may illuminate the cloth action behind the source image by reversal, since human covering here shuts out speech rather than sheltering its arrival.

luna: The section's duha is daylight radiance, while its lexicon allows a night illuminated like duha. This verse calls the moon light (نُورًا) and the sun a lamp (سِرَاجًا), articulating both sides of that brightness. | terra: The moon is made a light and the sun a lamp, pairing nocturnal illumination with the source of spreading daylight.
terra: The command to stand through the night except a little turns the time of settled rest into sustained recitation, the active boundary already explained by 73:6.

luna: The source calls night still and restful, while the assurance of 93:3 speaks within that quiet. This verse says the night rising (نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ) is more potent for speech, showing that night can intensify address as well as provide rest. | terra: Night's rising is described as firmer in impact and straighter for speech; it turns the time made for repose into wakeful recitation while retaining its special stillness.
terra: Day brings سَبْحًۭا طَوِيلًۭا, prolonged movement or occupation, which complements 73:6 and contrasts with the settled world heard in سَجَىٰ.
terra: God measures night and day while humans cannot keep exact account, a direct counterpart to the section's attention to rising, extension, and named degrees of daylight.
terra: The moon is sworn by just before the retreating night and brightening morning, contributing nocturnal light to that three-part transition.

luna: The source's night is dark and still, while the section as a whole turns from it toward daylight. This oath names night “when it retreats” (إِذْ أَدْبَرَ), presenting the boundary as night passing away. | terra: The oath to night إِذْ أَدْبَرَ shows the cover turning away, contrasting its motion with سَجَىٰ's stillness and leading into 74:34.

luna: The source gives morning light as the counterpart to settled night. “By the morning when it brightens” (وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا أَسْفَرَ) completes the retreating-night scene begun in 74:33. | terra: The oath to morning إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ stages brightness disclosed as night recedes, matching the lifting of the section's cover.

luna: The source describes the night as a covering and settled rest. Nearby, 78:10 calls night a garment; this verse's “sleep as rest” (النَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا) names the repose beneath that covering. | terra: Sleep is made سُبَاتًۭا, the repose that the next ayah's night-garment shelters and that 25:47 also joins to night.

luna: The source develops a secondary sense of سَجَىٰ as spreading cloth over something. “We made the night a garment” (وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا) gives that covering image a direct Quranic formulation. | terra: Night is made لِبَاسًۭا, the Quran's explicit realization of the section's image of cloth laid over the world.

luna: After 78:10's night garment, this verse says God made day “for livelihood” (النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا). It completes the adjacent night-to-day sequence with activity following the covered, resting time. | terra: Day is made مَعَاشًۭا after the night-garment of 78:10, giving the lifted cover its active, life-sustaining consequence.
luna: The source follows duha as sunlight spreading over the earth. This verse describes the sun as a “blazing lamp” (سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا), giving the daylight its source and force.

luna: The section defines ضحى as sunlight brought out into the lengthening day and pairs it with a night that settles over the world. Here “darkened its night” (أَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا) is answered by “brought out its ضحاها” (أَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا), making the alternation explicit. | terra: God darkens the sky's night and brings out its ضُحَىٰ, making the section's morning light something drawn forth from darkness.

luna: The section explicitly distinguishes the named hour ضحى from the light it describes. This verse pairs “an evening or its forenoon” (عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا) as a measure of how brief worldly life will seem; the time sense is direct, though the verse concerns resurrection rather than the daily light scene. | terra: Resurrection makes worldly duration seem only an evening or its ضُحَىٰ; the named morning hour becomes a measure of how quickly an apparently lasting interval passes.

luna: The source's night is a covering that settles over the world. This oath instead marks night as it withdraws or darkens (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ), offering a boundary reading of the same night cycle. | terra: The oath to night إِذَا عَسْعَسَ presents it withdrawing, a dynamic boundary to 93's settled night, and opens directly onto the breathing dawn of 81:18.

luna: The source sets night beside returning daylight. “By the morning when it breathes” (وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ) follows the night oath in 81:17 and gives the opening of light a vivid counterpart to night's cover. | terra: The oath to dawn إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ makes light breathe out after the retreating night, a close nonlexical parallel to the spread of ḍuḥā.
terra: Twilight is sworn by immediately before the gathering night of 84:17, preserving the visible threshold at which spreading day becomes cover.
terra: The oath to night وَمَا وَسَقَ presents night gathering and enclosing what it contains, close to the section's world closed over and stilled.
terra: The full moon is sworn by after the gathering night, giving a concrete Quranic instance for the source dictionary's secondary sense of a night bright like ḍuḥā.
terra: The oath by dawn names the first breach of night, an earlier boundary of the same morning light that rises and spreads into ḍuḥā.

luna: The section describes night as settled and enduring (سَكَنَ وَدَامَ in its lexical note). This oath names night when it moves on (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ), a specific boundary against the image of night at rest. | terra: The oath to night إِذَا يَسْرِ makes night travel away; that passing movement illuminates by contrast the persistence heard in سَجَىٰ.

luna: The source section's ضحى names both the forenoon and the sun's spreading light. This oath names “the sun and its ضحاها” (وَضُحَاهَا), directly joining the hour to its luminous source. | terra: The oath to the sun and its ضُحَىٰ names the same spreading morning light and gives the closest Quranic counterpart to 93:1.

luna: After the sun and its duha in 91:1, this oath names “the moon when it follows it” (وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَاهَا). It extends the source's day-to-night sequence into the next visible light. | terra: The moon follows the sun between the oath to its ḍuḥā and the oath to revealing day; it may support the bright-night branch of the image, though the ayah does not name night or moonlight.

luna: The section's daylight rises into view and echoes the daylight sense of the root noted for 93:10. Here “by the day when it displays it” (وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلَّاهَا) gives the sun's illumination a direct counterpart beside the sun-and-duha oath in 91:1. | terra: The oath to day إِذَا جَلَّىٰهَا says day displays the sun, spelling out the revealing spread implicit in ḍuḥā and completed by covering night in 91:4.

luna: The section stages duha first and a settled, covering night second. “By the night when it covers it” (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا) completes the sun sequence begun in 91:1 and makes the light-to-covering relation explicit. | terra: The oath to night إِذَا يَغْشَىٰهَا stages night covering the sun, directly matching the section's cloth-like closure over light.

luna: The source sets bright duha before the night that settles and covers. This oath starts with “the night when it covers” (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى), giving the same day-night image in the reverse order. | terra: The oath to night إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ repeats the covering action, while this surah places that covering night before the revealed day of 92:2.

luna: The source's sunlight spreads as day begins to lengthen. In the paired oath, “the day when it appears” (وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى) follows the covering night and makes the return of light the scene's second half. | terra: Day إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ becomes manifest after the covering night of 92:1, reversing 93's light-first order and showing the cover lift.
terra: Revelation is sent down during the Night of Decree, making night itself a setting of divine address rather than abandonment or empty silence.
terra: The night is better than a thousand months, explicitly denying that darkness or temporal stillness makes the interval empty or deficient.
terra: Angels and the Spirit descend in that night by their Lord's permission, giving concrete action and commanded presence within the still night named in 97:1.
terra: The night of 97:1 remains peace until the rising of dawn, so settled night has a stated boundary and ends without ceasing to be a gift.
terra: Calling God the Lord of ٱلْفَلَقِ presents daybreak itself as a divinely opened breach through darkness.
